SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JANUARY 22, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JANUARY 22, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was led by City Clerk Vida Barone.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by City of Cerritos Recreation Services Division,
  Youth Basketball League Team Rookie III – Dolphins.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations

  Proclamations were presented to:

  Micah Bendicion (Recognition of earning the rank of Eagle Scout).

  International Metal Source (Business Spotlight).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  C.W. Van der Linden suggested requiring delivery services to ring doorbells or
  leave packages where they are not visible from the street.

  Victor Manalo, Council Member, City of Artesia, provided an update on recent
  discussions and actions by the Southwest Regional Council and Southern
  California Association of Governments.

  John Watts spoke regarding the need for improved maintenance on specific
  freeway offramps and urged the City to advise Caltrans.

  Cheryl Davis spoke regarding crime, thanked Council for approving a resolution
  prohibiting parking on Denni Street, and asked for improved lighting in the area
  by removing select trees.
 City of Cerritos  January 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Herbie J. Pilato asked regarding future plans for the vacant lots on Carmenita
  Avenue and South Street and suggested the need for a family-friendly
  restaurant on the site.

  Gail Grossman expressed appreciation to the City for removing a tree from the
  parkway in front of her house.

  Yanet Lindner spoke regarding the need to review the City's overnight parking
  permit policy and suggested issuing hang tags for residents needing to park
  overnight.

  Mel Cortez spoke about the importance of showing mutual respect and concern
  for an increase in crime in the City.

  Jay Gray suggested providing regular safety updates during City Council
  meetings, televising the Community Safety Committee meetings, applying the
  revenues from the sale of the Cerritos/Astor Museum Collection towards public
  safety, implementing a public access channel to promote City events and to
  stopping funding of the Chamber of Commerce.

  Sam Desai offered a domain to the City, commented on the Cerritos/Astor
  Museum, suggested starting budget and finance discussions early in the process,
  and establish a triage to identify and provide to assistance to failing businesses.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke in opposition to the proposed Juliet Project and
  new zones to accommodate developers.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  January 11, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of January 11, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY.

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  January 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of Register Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 22,
  2018 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands dated January 22, 2018 in the total amount of
  $3,133,754.34 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer's Reports

  Approval of the City Council Treasurer’s report for the period ending December
  31, 2017 (COUNCIL).

  Approval of the Successor Agency Treasurer’s report for the period ending
  December 31, 2017 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council Treasurer’s report for the period ending December 31, 2017 and of
  the Successor Agency Treasurer’s report for the period ending December 31,
  2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Consideration of request for consent to the assignment of phase I and phase II
  ground leases (comprising main Cerritos Towne Center Retail parcels) and
  approval of an estoppel certificate in connection with the assignment of the
  referenced ground lease interests from Cerritos GARP LLC, a Delaware Limited
  Liability Company, to Cerritos TC Property LLC, a Delaware limited liability
  company, or another affiliate of Metropolitan Life Insurance Company, a New
  York Corporation who is approved by the City, for the primary retail component
  of the Cerritos Towne Center (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  January 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were
  no individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public hearing and
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to authorize the
  City Manager, or his designee, to execute the document(s) to facilitate,
  acknowledge and consent to the transfer of the ground leases of the Cerritos
  Towne Center retail component from GARP to Cerritos TC Property LLC, a
  Delaware limited liability company, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of
  Metropolitan Life Insurance Company and the Utah State Retirement Investment
  Fund, in such form as the City Manager shall deem appropriate, including any
  estoppel certificates, assignment consent, or related implementing
  documentation required or appropriate in connection with completion of such
  assignment in the forms attached with the agenda or such other form as the City
  Manager shall deem appropriate (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration by the City Council of the City of Cerritos of the
  disposition of the Cerritos/Astor Museum collection and authorization to enter
  into an agreement of sale (COUNCIL).

  A report was given by Jeff Thielke, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  John Watts spoke in opposition to the City holding an auction for the
  Cerritos/Astor Museum collection and in support of selling it to the Browning
  Automotive Group.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke regarding the cost of maintaining the
  Cerritos/Astor Museum collection, opined the City is losing money by selling it to
  the Browning Automotive Group and called for increased accountability.

  C.W. Van der Linden agreed with the previous speaker, questioned the
  legitimacy of the estimate, expressed concerns regarding the cost of maintaining
  the collection and spoke in support of selling the collection to the Browning
  Automotive Group.

  Mel Cortez spoke in support of the item and expressed concerns regarding City
  costs in maintaining the collection.
 City of Cerritos  January 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

8.  Public Hearings

8B.  (continued)

  Kent Browning commented on his experience with automobiles, noting he is an
  avid collector, expressed his interest and intent to maintain the collection in the
  City with the potential for public viewing and reported a minor problem with the
  title of one (1) vehicle that is in the process of being resolved.

  John Watts claimed Mr. Browning's offer is for the entire collection, not just the car
  collection, and spoke in support of the item.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke in support of the item.

  Kent Browning reported the deadline to submit an offer for the collection was
  December 31st, which he met. He felt that if someone else made an offer,
  today, it would not be fair to accept it as the deadline passed and they would
  know the amount of his offer.

  The Mayor closed the public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to extend the matter
  60 days for potential sale (no vote on motion due to substitute motion).

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to
  authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to negotiate the final terms and
  sale price, entering the City into an agreement of sale of the Cerritos/Astor
  Museum Collection for a minimum of $1,087,000 to Browning Automotive Group.

  Councilmember Pulido offered an amendment to the motion and Councilmember
  Edwards accepted the amendment, as follows:

  AMENDED SUBSTITUTE MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded
  by Pulido, to authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to negotiate the final
  terms and sale price, entering the City into an agreement of sale of the
  Cerritos/Astor Museum Collection for a minimum of $1,087,000 to Browning
  Automotive Group and to encourage Mr. Browning to arrange for public viewing
  and educational enrichment of the collection (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  Solanki, Hu
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Heritage Building Annex
  demolition, Bid No. 1329-17 (COUNCIL).

  A report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  January 22, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $270,599 for Heritage Building Annex
  Demolition (base bid and alternatives #1 and #2), Bid No. 1329-17, to
  BWW & Company and reject the other bids; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmember Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem Pulido,
  Councilmembers Solanki and Edwards, and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 10:36 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone_____________________
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

/s/Grace Hu_________________
